candidates.name: Viral myopericarditis
support_spans: She was admitted with a working diagnosis of viral myopericarditis.
Treatment with oral ibuprofen and colchicine resulted in resolution of chest pain, normalization of troponin and inflammatory markers, and reduction of the pericardial effusion over three days.
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results are consistent with viral myopericarditis, and the treatment with ibuprofen and colchicine led to improvement in symptoms and reduction of the pericardial effusion.

candidates.name: Loeffler syndrome
support_spans: Laboratory studies revealed a leukocyte count of 12,000 cells/µL with an absolute eosinophil count of 1,570 cells/µL (normal 40–190)
The absolute eosinophil count rose further
candidates.why: The patient's elevated eosinophil count and pulmonary nodules with ground-glass opacities are suggestive of Loeffler syndrome, a type of eosinophilic pneumonia.

candidates.name: Toxocariasis
support_spans: Further history elicited pica and exposure to two dogs and a cat
Toxocara serology was sent and was pending at discharge
candidates.why: The patient's history of pica and exposure to dogs and cats, along with the pending Toxocara serology, suggest the possibility of toxocariasis, a parasitic infection caused by Toxocara species.
